title: Weak hash function (MD5) — review required
description: A bare md5() call. MD5 is broken for security purposes (collisions are practical). It is unacceptable for passwords, signatures, or integrity of untrusted data, but still fine for non-security checksums. This lexical rule cannot tell the use case — treat every hit as review-required. Dotted method calls such as hashlib.md5() are covered by language-specific rules, not here.
remediation: Use SHA-256 or better for integrity; use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 for passwords. Keep MD5 only for non-security checksums (deduplication, etags) with a comment saying so.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches a bare md5( call regardless of purpose, and never matches dotted calls (hashlib.md5, Digest::MD5 style) — those belong to language-specific rules. SHA-1 and other weak algorithms are separate rules.
